_comment: SYNCED COPY. The source is ai-lab governance/payout-fields.json, which the JS chaser reads too. Edit it there, never here.
The one list of payment details a person can be chased for. Read by BOTH sides:
Python -- horilla-customizations renders the multi-select on the employee page from this.
JS     -- bin/lib/payroll-chase builds the chase messages and the filled check from this.
Two copies would drift, so there is exactly one and neither side hardcodes a field.
id       stable key stored in the chase row. NEVER renamed -- open chases hold it.
label    what the person clicking the button sees in the modal.
line     the plain-English line an agent reads in the email/text. 14-year-old bar.
spoken   unused today: the call clips are two fixed recordings that name no fields.
table    which Horilla table holds it: employee | bank.
column   the column, or additional_info.<key> for the jsonb blob.
rail     bank | wise | any -- which payout path the field belongs to.
Horilla has no column for place of birth, account type, name on account or the Wise
fields; onboarding already writes those into employee_employeebankdetails.additional_info,
so that is where they are read from. Do not invent a column on a table we do not own.

place_of_birth was REMOVED on 2026-09-20. Nothing in the company writes it: 0 of 161 bank rows carry the key and no form collects it. Leaving it tickable meant a chase that could never close -- the agent fills the form, the key is still absent, and they get chased to the 20-touch cap. If a bank ever needs it, add the form field FIRST, then put it back here.

Why it mattered: this field is blank for almost everyone, so it landed
in nearly every chase the week-before sweep would open. Pointed at a key
nobody writes, every one of those chases was UNRESOLVABLE -- the agent
fills the form, the form writes account_holder_name, the check still
reads empty, and they get called twice a day until the 20-touch cap.
